title: Adaptive Slew Throughput Harness for Multi-GPU TP/PP Regression Detection
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a reproducible, automated harness that exercises multi-GPU tensor-parallel (TP) and pipeline-parallel (PP) topologies under controlled slew-rate increases and jitter injection to detect throughput regressions (tokens/sec) and p95 latency drift. The harness should emphasize warmup profiles, KV-prefetch behavior, and cross-node burst characteristics so we can catch regressions introduced by kernel selection, scheduling heuristics, or KV cache regression bundles.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can sweep slew rates from 0.5x to 5x nominal QPS and produce stable aggregated metrics (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization) for TP/PP configurations
Automated regression detector flags statistically significant regressions using both histogram drift (Kolmogorov-Smirnov) and EWMA on p95 with configurable thresholds
Warm/cold-start separation is explicit: results must include separate windows for cold ramp, steady-state warmed with KV prefills, and a post-burst cooldown
Harness integrates with CI: nightly runs push summarized JSON + CSV artifacts and post to the runtime-telemetry Grafana dashboard and an S3 artifact bucket
Low flakiness target: false-positive rate < 3% on synthetic no-change baselines over 20 runs
test_plan: Build synthetic workload generator supporting mixed sequence lengths: short(32), mid(128), long(1024), with prefix-heavy distributions
Implement KV-prefill module to simulate warmed caches and a toggle to disable prefetch for cold experiments
Drive slew increases by ramping request injection rate at fixed intervals, add random jitter (0-20%) and periodic microbursts
Collect per-process histograms, GPU SM utilization, NVLink traffic, per-shard token/sec and per-request latencies
Run baseline ensemble (20 seeds) to establish control distributions, then run candidate builds and apply regression detector
Automate artifact collection: tar logs, perf counters, profiler flamegraphs, and aggregated metrics JSON
benchmark_configs: candidate_build: runtime-1.19-beta + kernel-set B (new attention kernel)
network: intra-node NVLink enabled, cross-node InfiniBand RDMA enabled with 4 lanes
node_spec: p4d-equivalent, 8 GPUs per machine, 100Gbps interconnect
regression_detection: Primary: EWMA on p95 with alpha=0.2 and alert if > 8% sustained over 3 windows
Secondary: Two-sample KS test on tokens/sec distribution vs baseline (p<0.01 triggers investigation)
Outlier gating: Tukey fence on per-shard p95 to avoid single-shard flares causing global alerts
Composite score: weighted sum of normalized tokens/sec drop, p95 increase, and KV_hit_ratio loss
Alert outputs: human-readable summary, top-5 contributing metrics, link to artifacts and flamegraphs
results_summary: 2026-03-08 preliminary: candidate_build showed a 6.5% drop in global tokens/sec for the large topology under 3x slew with EWMA signal crossing threshold
Per-shard analysis pointed to PP stage 3 experiencing 2-3x higher queue wait times; NVLink counters showed elevated stall cycles
KV-prefill disabled runs had 12% worse p95 compared to warmed runs, confirming KV-prefetch sensitivity
False positives: observed one KS-triggered alert in baseline ensemble due to seed-specific microburst alignment; tuning reduced FP rate to ~2.5%
Nightly CI integration validated: harness ran in 7h for full large-topology sweep and produced deterministic summary artifacts
infra_footprint: Staging cluster: 6 nodes (48 GPUs) for parallel topologies; ephemeral build runners for each candidate
Storage: S3 bucket redwood-bench-artifacts/eng-88190, retention 90 days
CI: Jenkins pipeline job runtime-throughput/harness-nightly, parallel shards per topology
Monitoring: Grafana dashboard runtime-throughput/eng-88190, Alertmanager rule group eng-88190-regressions
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Long-running harness may be noisy and expensive; Mitigation: run medium+large topologies staggered and use cheaper small-topology smoke tests for quick feedback
Risk: Non-determinism from network jitter causes false positives; Mitigation: include network-normalized baseline and synthetic jitter injection to make detector robust
Risk: Detector too sensitive to model variance across seeds; Mitigation: require composite score exceedance and repeat across >=2 seeds before firing actionable alert
